doc.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022

title: Opening and keeping trumpet chops up through Covid
summary: Rowe introduces Weiss; Weiss says the pandemic years were up and down, with his mother's death and clearing out the Queens family house taking over, plus a stretch of months not playing.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive at Hamilton College. I’m very pleased to have David Weiss with me today who is a composer, arranger, band leader, and, according to Jazz Times has righteous trumpet chops.
That goes back a ways, a review.
Maybe they’re not so righteous anymore.
Well I’m just — I’m wondering if you’re able to keep your trumpet chops up during this almost two years of Covid now?

It’s been interesting. It’s been interesting. Yes and no. I mean it’s been two years and there’s been a lot of up and downs and there’s been things in my personal life that I let take everything over because — I suppose they do — my mother passed away a little over two years ago, the house we grew up in in Queens is a big houses and it took months and months to clean it out. So, with no gigs, I let that other stuff take over, you know, the last few months. But other times I went away for a while and was able to practice more than I had practiced in years. Right after that low point of not playing at all for the first time in my life for like three or four months I think it was. Then I was able to go somewhere and basically have a place to play all the time and practice more than I had for several weeks.
